verbalization: Chlorpromazine, a phenothiazine antipsychotic, is directly linked to Calm1 through a series of molecular interactions. The evidence suggests that Chlorpromazine, as part of the phenothiazine class, binds to Calm1, a key receptor involved in regulating neural activity and mood. This binding is supported by the hierarchical relationships in the dataset, where Chlorpromazine and Fluphenazine are both classified under the broader category of phenothiazines, which in turn binds to Calm1. The lowest common ancestor of these entities is Phenothiazines, reinforcing the central role of this class in the interaction. The integration of these pathways highlights a mechanism by which Chlorpromazine exerts its effects on Calm1, potentially influencing neural signaling and contributing to its therapeutic properties.
